Issued at 256 PM CDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Bufkit soundings indicate a persistent, shallow layer of low stratus 
clouds for the remainder of today. Clouds will likely limit our 
highs somewhat from what the NBM loaded, adjusted down slightly with 
a blend of NBM/CONSShort. Overnight lows will fall to the 40s. 

Meanwhile a southern stream upper trough located over the central 
Rockies will work east through the rest of today. Early this evening 
the trough and associated surface low will eject out onto the 
central plains and then accelerate northeast. As it does so 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will form over western 
Nebraska and Kansas. These will move northeast with the system and 
begin to impact south central South Dakota between roughly 6 and 8 
pm CDT tonight. Scattered showers and storms should be in the Sioux 
Falls area roughly between 10 pm and midnight. As the surface low 
skirts just to the south of the CWA early Thursday morning showers 
and storms become more numerous, especially for areas along and 
south of I-90 and into northwest Iowa. Here a few stronger storms 
may produce more frequent lightning and isolated pockets of heavy 
rain. Severe weather is not anticipated.  

Late Thursday morning into the afternoon a northern stream upper 
trough and surface low will move into central Canada. A cold front 
will form off of this low and will pass through the region from the 
northwest to the southeast. Behind the front storms end and clouds 
begin to break up Thursday afternoon and into the evening. 
Simultaneously the northern stream wave extends south, eventually 
phasing into the southern stream wave. This will result in an 
amplifying effect as the now deep amplitude upper trough tightens 
and narrows. Thursday evening the LLJ responds to this amplification 
by ramping quickly up to 50+ mph. These strong winds will mix down 
resulting in surface gusts of 30 to 40 mph. Occasional gusts as
high as 45 mph are also possible over central South Dakota. Our
western most counties may briefly approach Wind Advisory 
criteria late Thursday evening, but guidance is not in good 
agreement at this time. As such, have opted to wait on a wind 
headline at this time. Winds generally decrease as you move to 
the east but will remain gusty at 25-35 mph. The stronger winds 
gradually move east overnight into Friday morning. Additional 
wind concerns will be along the lee side of Buffalo Ridge where 
additional gusts of 40+ mph are possible.

As far as rain totals are concerned the latest guidance has trended 
down a little. Areas along Highway 14 and north will only see a 
trace up to a tenth or two. As you move south toward I-90 totals 
increase to a couple tenths up to 0.30 inches. For areas along and 
south of I-90 guidance indicates rain totals ranging from 0.25 to 
0.75 inches, with highest totals focused over northwest Iowa. Areas 
along and south of Highway 20 may see isolated pockets up to 1 inch. 

Breezy winds continue into early Friday afternoon before gradually 
tapering off Friday evening. Friday highs will be on the cool side 
of climatology thanks to strong CAA on northwesterly winds, in the 
low to mid 50s. Skies clear through the day and remain clear through 
the overnight. This will allow for maximum radiational cooling, 
resulting in low temperatures by sunrise Saturday in the low to mid 
30s. Area of frost are possible, mainly west of the James River 
Valley. Clear skies continue for Saturday as winds turn southerly 
and usher in warmer air. Highs will climb  into the low to upper 
60s, warmest over central South Dakota. No concerns at this time for 
frost Saturday night into Sunday morning with lows in the 40s. 
Sunday will be another mostly clear day with continued WAA. Highs 
will climb into the mid to upper 60s with lows in the 40s. Dry 
conditions and highs in the 60s and low 70s continue into the first 
half of next week.
